newsitem.title: UK: Lower world imports to weigh on EU sugar producers.
newsitem.headline: Lower world imports to weigh on EU sugar producers.

text.p: European Union (EU) sugar producers should bear the brunt of a forecast fall in world imports and also face regional competition from the new Middle East refineries, statistician F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.

In its first estimate of the global sugar balance for 1996/97 (September/August), Licht said the white sugar sector had most reason to be concerned about the forecast imports fall of 1.98 million tonnes.

"Not only is import demand in the developing countries likely to fall...but in Europe, Turkey and ex-Yugoslavia will need much less while the Russian government has taken active steps to deter white sugar imports by raising taxes and duties."
Licht said developing countries mainly imported white sugar. World 1996/97 imports were pegged at 35.41 million tonnes.
But the new sugar refineries in the Middle East would have the most significant effect on European producers, it added.
Dubai's refinery is already operating while commercial production is expected to commence at the Jeddah plant in the first quarter of 1997.

"These refineries will have a capacity in excess of one million tonnes and as they will produce high quality sugar of European standard it will presumably be the EU producers, China and to an extent the US in-transit refiners who will feel the brunt of their impact," Licht said.
